article.headline: A Blender Add-on That Turns Any Mesh into Volumetric Clouds
article.lede: Generating believable clouds in 3D software has long been one of the more tedious corners of environment art. Cloud Generator V2, a free add-on for Blender, collapses that work into a single operator: select a mesh, press convert, and the tool wraps it in *volumetric* geometry. The result is a sky-ready cloud whose silhouette the artist already sculpted.
article.body:
The workflow exploits a straightforward insight: the hardest part of cloud-making is controlling the overall shape, and that's exactly what mesh modeling is already good at. An artist can block out a cumulus form using Blender's standard tools — or, as the demo shows, start from Suzanne, the software's iconic monkey-head test mesh — and then hand it off to the add-on. What comes back is a **volumetric object** (a cloud rendered as a participating medium, simulating how light scatters through water droplets) that inherits that custom silhouette.

The add-on is built primarily for *Cycles*, Blender's physically-based path-tracing render engine. Cycles handles volumetrics well because it models individual light rays bouncing through a medium; the competing in-house engine, *EEVEE*, uses rasterization shortcuts that make convincing volumetrics harder to achieve. The add-on offers basic EEVEE compatibility, but the showcase imagery relies on Cycles.

The tool's hashtags — `#geometrynode`, `#geonodes` — suggest it is built on Blender's *Geometry Nodes* system, a node-based procedural framework introduced in Blender 2.92 that lets artists construct and modify geometry through visual programming rather than hand-modelling. That lineage matters: it means the cloud output is likely non-destructive and adjustable through exposed node parameters rather than baked geometry.

Cloud Generator V2 is distributed free via Gumroad and is catalogued on BlendAtlas. For game developers working in Unreal Engine 5 (the UE5 tag in the post) or film artists needing hero sky elements, the add-on addresses a real bottleneck: procedural sky systems excel at background atmosphere but give little control over individual cloud placement and shape. A mesh-derived cloud fills that gap.

concepts.definition: A technique that simulates how light travels through semi-transparent media like smoke, fog, or clouds by modelling the scattering and absorption of individual light rays. Unlike surface rendering, which only computes light at an object's skin, volumetric rendering treats the interior of an object as a light-interacting medium, producing the soft, glowing quality of real clouds.

A node-based procedural system inside Blender that lets artists build, transform, and instance geometry through a visual graph rather than by hand-modelling. Changes to the graph propagate automatically, keeping the workflow non-destructive. It was introduced in Blender 2.92 and has become central to procedural art pipelines.

Cycles is Blender's physically-based path-tracer: it simulates light transport accurately, handles volumetrics and caustics well, but is computationally slow. EEVEE is Blender's real-time rasterization engine: far faster and suited to game-style previews, but it uses screen-space approximations that struggle with complex volumetric effects.

A discipline in 3D and digital art where visual results are generated by algorithms and parameter sets rather than manual authoring of every detail. Procedural workflows are prized for their repeatability, scalability, and the ease with which large-scale or randomised content can be produced without rebuilding assets from scratch.
